extracted.intended_audience: students/readers of elementary plane geometry and readers of historical mathematical texts
extracted.subtask_description: An OCR'd Italian excerpt of a classical Euclidean-style plane geometry treatise containing definitions, common notions, and elementary propositions and constructions (angle bisector, perpendiculars, triangle congruence, circle definitions, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic geometric definitions (point, line, plane, surface)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of fundamental terms: point (termini), straight line (linea recta), curved line (linea curva), plane surface (superfice pia), plane figure, multi-sided figure (poligono), circumference and center of a circle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains that lines terminate in points, distinguishes straight from curved lines (recta vs curva), defines plane figures by their bounding lines, and defines a circle as having a center and circumference; these are treated as the foundational vocabulary used in subsequent constructions and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of circle (center, diameter, circumference)
rubrics_metrics.description: A circle is described with a center and circumference; diameter and radius notions are given (centro, circonferentia, diametro).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that every circle has a center from which all radii to the circumference are equal; mentions relations between center, circumference, diameter and uses these in later constructions (e.g., drawing circles, intersections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Euclid's common notions about equality (transitivity, addition/subtraction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements asserting equality principles: things equal to the same are equal to each other; equals added to equals are equal; equals subtracted from equals leave equals; multiplicative/ratio equality behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are presented as general arithmetic/logical rules (common notions) that underlie geometric equalities and are invoked in proofs (e.g., if segments or angles are equal pairwise then combined segments/angles are equal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction: to make an equilateral triangle on a given line
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a straight line segment, construct an equilateral triangle upon it (fa vno triangolo equilateral e...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classical construction (compass-and-straightedge) is stated as a basic construction used later for other constructions and proofs; the surrounding text sketches the method using circles centered at endpoints and their intersection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction: to bisect an angle (divide an angle into equal parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an angle, construct a line that divides it into two equal angles (vno angolo Io quale voglio diuidere ... per meco aoe p igualparti).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives the proposition and outlines the construction technique (using arcs and intersections) and notes it as a routine Euclidean construction used frequently in further propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction: to divide a given straight line into equal parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a straight line, construct points on it so that it is divided into two (or more) equal parts (vna linea retta la qìe voglio diuidere 1.2 parti iguali).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology is sketched (using circles/copying segments) and used as a building block for other constructions (e.g., constructing mediators, centers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction: to draw a perpendicular from a point to a given line
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a line and a point (either on or off the line), construct a perpendicular from the point to the line (menare vna perpendiculare).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two cases are treated: point on the line and point not on the line; procedures (compass and straightedge) are indicated and used to produce right angles and perpendiculars needed in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying an angle at a given point on a line (angle transfer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an angle and a segment of a line, construct at that segment's endpoint an angle equal to the given angle (fare vno angolo iguali a vno angolo dato sulla linea data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure relies on transporting arc lengths and constructing intersections to reproduce an angle; used to create congruent figures and in congruence proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triangle congruence criteria (SAS, ASA, SSS, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several propositions about equality/congruence of triangles: if two sides and the included angle of one triangle equal two sides and included angle of another, the triangles are equal; if two angles and a side correspond, triangles are equal; if three sides of one equal three sides of another, triangles are equal; and related corollaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text states these as foundational congruence results, proves them with classical geometric reasoning and then uses them to deduce equalities of corresponding angles and sides in later propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isosceles triangle base angles equality and related results
rubrics_metrics.description: If two sides of a triangle are equal (an isosceles triangle), then the angles opposite those sides are equal; conversely, if two angles are equal, the opposite sides are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as a basic theorem with proof and used to deduce further equalities and constructions (e.g., finding base angles or bisecting vertex angles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Angle and parallelism relations (equal and equidistant lines, alternates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propositions about equal/equidistant straight lines and the angles they produce: when lines are equidistant and certain lines meet them, resulting corresponding angles are equal; alternate-interior angle relationships underlie parallelism arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats equidistant lines and equal angles as geometric tools; it shows how equalities of angles or distances imply parallelism or other alignment properties used in constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum and comparison properties of triangle angles
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements about magnitudes of triangle angles (e.g., relations that two angles of a triangle are together less/greater than certain right angles; various inequalities among triangle angles are asserted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These propositions are given with accompanying reasoning; exact modern formulations may be distributed across several numbered items in the text (inequalities and comparisons are used in later deductions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and comparison using circles and equal radii (intersection method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of circles (centred at given points with equal radii) to create intersections that yield equal segments or angles (e.g., producing points equidistant from endpoints to build perpendicular bisectors or equilateral triangles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the recurring geometric technique in many constructions: draw circles of equal radius about given endpoints and use their intersection(s) to define new vertices; the treatise repeatedly uses this for basic constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural remark: emulate Euclid with practical/visual proofs rather than extensive algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: The author emphasizes constructing and demonstrating properties by geometric diagrams and elementary manipulations (circles, straightedge), often reducing complexity by avoiding heavy algebraic machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prefatory remarks indicate the text aims to be practical/geometric for 'pratica geometrica' and agrimensoria (surveying), prioritizing constructive procedures and clear figures; proofs are shown as constructions and demonstrations within that tradition.
